subject: Post-demo: Competitive bake-off sprint plan & owners
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-30T14:05:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: Competitive bake-off sprint plan & owners

Thanks again for the demo time today — great conversation. Short recap and a proposed sprint plan so we all have the same next steps.

Call highlights (SaaSBeta priorities):
- Latency (p95) at interactive payloads ~1k tokens is the top non-negotiable (target: <= 300ms).
- Unit cost / token and predictable burst capacity for peak times.
- Output fidelity / hallucination rate on our critical prompt sets.
- Enterprise controls: KMS-backed key management, SOC 2 evidence, and audit logs.

Proposed two-week bake-off sprint (high level):
1) Test scope: latency/throughput benchmarks, cost-per-1k tokens analysis, fidelity/regression on a curated 10‑prompt eval set, and reliability under burst.
2) Baselines: Hyperscaler endpoints (listed: Bedrock/Vertex + target open inference APIs) — we will run identical traffic profiles.
3) Success criteria (examples to confirm): p95 latency <= 300ms at median throughput, cost delta <= 25% vs chosen hyperscaler for the same QoS, and >=95% pass rate on red-team prompt set (we'll align exact scoring).
4) Timeline & owners:
   - Benchmark harness + scripts: Ben Carter (Redwood) — due Dec 4
   - Private trial / deployment config (VPC/KMS): Vivek Kulkarni (Redwood) — trial ready by Dec 6
   - Procurement / PO / contract coordination: Marissa Cole (Redwood) — draft PO by Dec 3
   - Dataset & eval prompts: Alex / Priya (SaaSBeta) — sample by Dec 3

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff_spec.xlsx (test cases, traffic profiles, data format), quickbench PDF with example baselines.

Questions for you: please confirm (1) that the timelines above work, (2) any additional success criteria we should include, and (3) whether the eval set needs any additional anonymization steps.

Soojin

Date: 2026-11-30T17:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Competitive bake-off sprint plan & owners

Appreciate the clear plan, Soojin — this looks like the right shape. A few quick items from our side: 

- Timeline: two-week sprint is fine. Dec 3 dataset delivery is OK but we'll need to anonymize customer IDs; we can deliver CSV + prompt mapping.
- Success criteria: prioritize p95 latency above cost (if tradeoffs needed we choose latency). Also add deterministic output flag for a subset of prompts (we need repeatability).
- KMS: can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed keys for private deployments? We will need that for compliance.

We can provide a sample of 250 real-ish prompts (anonymized) and a small truth set for fidelity checks. We'd like a minimal set of API credentials for Redwood so we can validate calls from our side in parallel (short-lived credentials).

On the hyperscaler baselines: we'll share our reference endpoints (Bedrock / Vertex) and their current benchmark numbers in a follow-up email. Looking forward to Ben's harness.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Infrastructure & AI Strategy
Hyperscale-Pro (partner to SaaSBeta)

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Competitive bake-off sprint plan & owners

Thanks — looping in more detail on the harness and runs. See plan below (I copied the spec skeleton into the attached).

Bench plan (Ben Carter):
- Harness: JMeter + custom runner that replays tokens using identical prompt/seed pairs. Will produce per-request latencies, token counts, and cost estimators. Output: CSV + JSON summary.
- Workloads: 3 profiles (interactive chat 1k tokens, batch 5k-token bulk, and burst 200 concurrent short requests).
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95 latency, tail error rates, tokens-per-second, synthesized cost (matching each vendor's pricing model).
- Fidelity tests: a 10-prompt golden set with manual grading (Pass/Fail/Partial) — need SaaSBeta truth set.
- Repro runs: 3 runs per config, average + variance reported.

Baseline targets (examples we will compare to):
- Hyperscaler A (Bedrock): p95 320ms (interactive profile) — we will measure delta.
- Hyperscaler B (Vertex): p95 280ms.

Deliverables & dates: harness ready and smoke-tested (Dec 4), first Redwood vs hyperscaler run (Dec 6–7), consolidated results (Dec 9).

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff_spec.xlsx (skeleton), redwood_vs_hyperscaler_quickbench.pdf (sample numbers).

--
